region.text: Kollam (Venad), the 'formidable rulers of Kollam'

ledger.note: c. 1005: the Cholas hold Kollam (Venad) and southern Kerala. The Senur inscription (1005 on the page) lists 'defeating the formidable rulers of Kollam (Venad)'; 'The Chola subjugation of Kerala can be dated to the early years of the 11th century'; Kandalur Salai 'around 988' is a naval victory, not a gain.

region.text: the southern Kalinga coast, the Chola northern boundary in Rajaraja's time

ledger.note: c. 1010 (bridge): Rajaraja I's Kalinga invasion. 'The invasion of the kingdom of Kalinga occurred after the conquest of Vengi', marking 'the northern boundary of the Chola Empire at that time'. The page gives no year; Cliopatria draws the Chola shape to the Kalinga coast from 1010 and Rajaraja reigned to 1014. Page silent on the year. The counterpart eastern-ganga-kingdom is my reading: the page names only 'the kingdom of Kalinga'.

region.text: the whole island: 'the conquest of Anuradhapura was completed in the 36th year' of Rajaraja's reign (c. 1017-18); the Polonnaruwa kingdom invaded in 1017

ledger.note: 1017: Rajendra I completes the conquest of Sri Lanka. 'in 1016, Rajendra sent a naval force to Sri Lanka and brought the Ruhuna Kingdom under his control'; 'Rajendra invaded the Kingdom of Polonnaruwa in the south in 1017'; the captured Mahinda V 'died in exile in 1029'. The Sinhalese held out in Rohana (Kassapa VI reigned there 1029-1040) until Vijayabahu's rising of 1070.

ledger.note: 1018: Rajendra I takes the Maldives and Lakshadweep. 'In 1018, Rajendra's forces captured the Maldives and Lakshadweep islands.' No Cliopatria shape includes the islands; the page does not say when the Cholas lost them.

'In 1018 and 1019 CE, Rajendra invaded and conquered the Pandya and Chera Perumal kingdoms' and 'appointed one of his sons as viceroy ... in charge of both Pandya and Chera/Kerala' (Rajendra Chola I page); the Chera Perumals were 'attacked and eventually forced into submission by the Cholas in c. early 11th century CE' yet the dynasty is dated 'c. 844 CE-c. 1124 CE' with a last ruler 'c. 1089-1124', and 'In the early 12th century, the medieval Chera kingdom of Kerala dissolved into several local powers' (Chera Perumals page). Repair fx-28: retyped from gain to vassal_start (F290): a gain would hand the whole of Kerala to the Cholas for a century although the Chera dossier keeps its kings and its Kerala keyframe 1001-1124, and records the war of 1097-1102 for Kollam; data/hierarchy.csv already has the Chera as a Chola vassal for 1005-1096.

Cliopatria already draws the Pandya country as Chola from 922, so the page's conquest of 1018-19 implies either that the Pandyas had recovered it or that the page describes a reassertion; the page does not say.

notes:
CHOLA EMPIRE (sa-03-e). 9 pages opened (the budget); every verdict, event and war cites one of them. Facts come from WebFetch extractions of the dated sentences; where a page was silent the event is confidence 1 or the keyframe says 'unverified: page budget' / 'page silent'.

Cliopatria rows: one row (27 shapes, 850-1259); the dynasty runs 848-1279, so two new keyframes (848-849 and 1260-1279) were added. The infobox gives no area (only 'greatest extent: 1030'), so no area sanity check was possible.

Disagreements between pages: (1) Pandya invasion/Thirupurambiyam 878 (Aditya I) vs 'defeated the Pandyan dynasty of Madurai in 885' (Chola Empire); (2) Sri Lanka 'In 925, Parantaka I conquered Sri Lanka' (Chola Empire) vs a raid 'around 946-947' (Parantaka I) vs the conquest 993-1017 (Rajaraja I, Rajendra I); (3) Vengi becomes a province after Vijayaditya's death in 1075 (Chola Empire) vs 1077 (Kulottunga I); (4) Gangavadi lost 1116 (Hoysala page) vs 'around 1118' (Chola Empire, Later Cholas); (5) Srivijaya crossing 1023 vs 1025 on the Rajendra page itself; (6) Pandya Empire page says Jatavarman Sundara I subdued 'Rajendra II' c. 1258-60, which can only be Rajendra III (reign 1256-1279).

Gaps for a gap-filler: the far south (Tirunelveli) in Cliopatria's 936-959 and 970-999 shapes; the Chola hold on the Maldives and Lakshadweep after 1018 (no page gives an end, so the islands stay Chola until the dissolve); Kalinga after 1010 and the Eastern Gangas (Chodaganga); who took Vengi and the north in 1177; the 1241 and 1236 contractions; the Hoysala and Kakatiya share of the Chola north after 1250; the capital between 1025 and 1279; the years of the Vengi protectorate before 1075 (the Rajaraja page contradicts itself on who held Vengi in 1006). Suggested pages: Parantaka II, Uttama Chola, Rajadhiraja I, Virarajendra Chola, Kulottunga III, Rajaraja III, Eastern Chalukyas, Chera Perumals of Makotai, Kakatiya dynasty, Ganapati Deva.

Counterparts needing dossiers: muttaraiyar, eastern-chalukyas, chera-perumal-kingdom, venad, and a Pandya state for the 920s-1216 (pandya-dynasty ends 915 in its dossier, pandya-empire starts 1216). Gazetteer names needed: Tondaimandalam, Kongu Nadu, Vengi, Rattapadi, Gangavadi, Nolambavadi, Rohana/Ruhuna, Rajarata, Kadaram. The regions here are approximated by place radii (Kanchipuram 110 km, Rajahmundry 130 km + Vijayawada 110 km, Mysuru/Bengaluru/Kolar, Kollam 100 km, Kedah 60 km + Palembang 80 km).
